newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacia sees more restructuring charges possible.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia sees more restructuring charges possible.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said it may report more, unspecified restructuring charges against earnings this year on a manufacturing rationalization program.

In a conference call on Wednesday, chief financial officer Robert Salisbury said, "Looking forward into 1997 and 1998, there may be some additional restructuring charges related to our manufacturing rationalization program that we call Supply 2000. We'll be making an announcement later in the year as to what we expect those might be."

The London-based drugs manufacturer -- formed 16 months ago from the merger of Upjohn Co, of Kalamzaoo, Mich., and Sweden's Pharmacia AB -- reported after-tax restructuring charges and other non-recurring items of $436 million in 1996 and $201 million in 1995.

The company said Wednesday that net sales for 1996 were $7.2 billion, compared to 1995 net sales of $6.9 billion. For the fourth quarter, sales totalled $1.9 billion, up 7.5 percent from the year-ago period.
That quarterly sales growth rate was distorted by a special promotional program, Salisbury said.
"We've suggested that the impact could be as much as two percentage points of the 7.5 percent," Salisbury said.

"Once you take away that impact, then I think it provides a more reasonable approximation or trendline that people might take into 1997 ... Growth in the range of 5.5 percent would be a more realistic representation of what occured in the fourth quarter of 1996. We'll let the experts on forecasting decide how to translate that into a forecast for 1997," he said.
Pharmacia & Upjohn is being less exact this year in providing Wall Street analysts with guidance on its profit outlook, he added.
"We might expect that there could be some adjustment in the estimates that some analysts might choose to make as a result of that," Salisbury said.
